parsed.explanation: The division is comparatively low-risk locally: no facility ban, no state gender-affirming-care ban, a veto record against restrictions, and patchwork nondiscrimination. But the combined regime is dominated by the parent national border and custody framework: passport sex-marker restrictions, halted X markers, confiscation/stranding reports, refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings, and documented abuse in immigration custody. Local tolerance does not cancel federal entry screening or detention. A trans adult travelling alone faces the border exposure every crossing; an adult with a trans minor additionally faces national care-funding pressure and school-transition threat framing, partly offset locally by the state's lack of a care ban and its litigation against national health rules.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport sex-marker restrictions; X markers not processed for new issues; reports of confiscated/blocked passports and stranded travellers; discrepancy can trigger refusal or possible lifetime fraud finding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is under litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists. Division marker-change rules are restrictive but visitor uses home passport.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening is national; no division law shields a visitor from federal document or fraud findings.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; corrections policies include conversion-style practices. Suspicion at border can lead to detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Fraud finding is never automatic and requires four elements; court challenges and legal-aid guidance exist.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: National custody rules apply regardless of division protections; local low-risk label does not bind federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; national facilities may apply. Some states criminalise bathroom use, but not this division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division has no law barring facility use consistent with gender identity and no sex-definition law; governor vetoed related restrictions.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local facility tolerance does not cancel national facility rules in federal or federally funded settings.

care_services.exposure: National funding pressure and proposed health rules; two hospital systems paused youth pharmacologic care after national payment threat. National care restrictions affect minors.
care_services.protection: Division has no ban on gender-affirming care; governor vetoed care bans; state justice department joined challenge to national health declaration. Adult care not documented as banned.
care_services.interaction: National payment policy reaches local hospitals even without a state ban; local challenge may limit but is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; executive order directs investigation of schools facilitating social transition; official hostility documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have blocked several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing can affect policing and schools; division has no equivalent state campaign.

minors_guardians.exposure: National executive order frames youth gender-affirming care as mutilation and threatens prosecution over social transition; care bans in many states and national insurance rules target minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Division has no youth care ban; governor vetoed one; state joined challenge. Local hospital pause flows from national funding pressure, not state law.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting adult with a trans minor faces national care and school-transition exposure; local protections are partial and cannot override federal funding or border rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide gender-identity hate-crime protection; only patchwork local ordinances; prosecutors sometimes use perceived sexual orientation as route for gender-identity-motivated crimes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State executive order bars discrimination in state employment, contracting and services; 21% live under full local ordinances; police gender-omission practice. National hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local protections vary by city; a visitor outside covered cities has thinner recourse, while national hate-crime law remains theoretical.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy is in effect; border refusal may strand travellers; litigation outcomes and waiver availability unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, legal-aid FAQ, state challenge to national health declaration, and court injunctions against some orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are national and slow; division cannot bind border officers or federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar entry-denial and document-confiscation exposure, but this regime adds national passport-marker restrictions, possible lifetime fraud findings and documented immigration-custody abuse. Local division tolerance is better than 0.35-A, but it does not reach the border, so the combined score sits slightly below.

0.55-B shows a functioning transit guideline and supervisor intervention preventing detention. Here no equivalent border protection is documented, and national screening can refuse entry or feed custody; hence materially lower.
0.75-C has an operating patient-privacy directive and local resolution. This division has no care ban and local tolerance, but national border, funding and custody rules dominate; it is much lower.

0.25-B involves coercive custody and extortion with no institutional protection. This case has a comparatively protective local division and no state facility ban, but national border refusal and custody abuse are documented; it rates near the upper end of that band, not above it.

parsed.synthesis: Locally, the division is one of the less restrictive environments: no bathroom ban, no state care ban, vetoes against restrictions, and some municipal protections. But the traveller cannot avoid the national border, document regime, or federal custody. A passport mismatch can mean public questioning, refusal, possible fraud findings, or detention with documented abuse. The division's protections operate after entry and do not bind federal actors. A lone adult faces this at every crossing; a family with a trans minor also faces national care-funding and school-transition pressure, only partly offset by local policy.
